To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) binding affinity can, by itself, shape the localization of antibodies within tumors; (2) the rate of dissociation from antigen can determine internalization and degradation; and (3) strategies to increase avidity can be more effective than simply increasing affinity.
affinity and avidity are key factors that influence antibody localization and efficacy in tumor tissue.

1) affinity and avidity can both be critical determinants of antibody efficacy in tumor targeting and 2) the relative importance of these factors is highly dependent on the specific application and the properties of the antibody and its antigen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of antibody-based therapies for cancer.
the design of antibodies that target tumors.
how antibody affinity and avidity can shape the efficacy of antibody-based cancer therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
affinity and avidity are both important and that the relative importance of each is dependent upon the antibody, antigen, and tumor type being targeted.
affinity and avidity are critical factors in tumor targeting that should be considered in the design and optimization of therapeutic and diagnostic antibodies.
the affinity and avidity relationship between antibodies and tumor antigens is a key factor in the design of successful antibody-based tumor-targeting strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
affinity and avidity are critical factors in the success of antibody-based tumor targeting, but their roles are complicated by the complexity of the tumor microenvironment.
avidity and affinity are critical factors in tumor targeting, but their effects are highly dependent on the tumor tissue, the antibody, and the target.

the binding affinity of an antibody to a target can dictate the localization of the antibody in the tumor and, therefore, can influence efficacy, while the avidity of the antibody can influence the specificity and efficacy of targeting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the affinity and avidity are not independent variables.
the affinity and avidity relationship is complex and that a careful balance of these two properties is necessary to optimize the efficacy of antibody-based therapies.
the relationship between an antibody and the antigen it targets is critical to understanding the dynamics of antibody-based tumor targeting and that this relationship is complex and multifaceted.
